rationale: The agent found that the split is by pair, not by protein: every test pair shares a protein with training and 99% share both. It showed that a per-protein label-rate baseline with no features reaches AUROC 0.82, warned that this split mainly rewards memorizing protein propensities, and used a protein-disjoint evaluation (about 0.64) as the figure to expect on new proteins. It did not accept the random-split performance as evidence of generalization.
